text:
maria.p: quick follow-up from the loader RFC — thinking about a 'progressive hydration' refactor to unify streaming safetensor shards, tile-based sharding, and warmup lanes. sketch below, want quick gut-checks.

sanjay.k: curious, what does 'progressive hydration' buy us vs the current prefetch/prefill model? is this just naming or a real api change?

maria.p: real change. instead of a single warmup pass we expose a hydration pipeline: descriptor -> thin index -> prioritized tile fetch -> materialize. allows on-demand zero-copy mmap for large tiles and async quantized decode for small ones.

kevin_h: sounds promising. i like the separation: descriptors give placement & affinity info, hydration pipeline does io/transform. we should define a tiny async interface:

kevin_h: ```
interface DescriptorStream { next(): Promise<Descriptor> }
interface Hydrator { hydrate(desc): Promise<Handle> // returns token/handle for eviction
``` 

ana: interface looks clean. few tradeoffs: 1) device memory accounting when materialize is async, 2) ordering guarantees for kv-cache priming, 3) observability for partial hydration failures.

maria.p: yep on all. thinking hydration handles carry a 'priority' and 'lane' field. lanes = {hot, warm, cold}. hot lane = immediate synchronous materialize; warm = async decode+transfer; cold = metadata-only until explicit demand.

sanjay.k: how do we represent safetensor shard indexes? single manifest per checkpoint or streaming manifest embedded in the first shard?

maria.p: propose 'checkpoint envelope' meta: lightweight streamable manifest (protobuf-lite) in the checkpoint header. loader can read header (few KB) then stream descriptors. avoids full manifest roundtrip for big model stores.

kevin_h: love streamable manifest. also consider manifestless mode where descriptors are derived from shard headers on the fly — useful for S3-range friendly stores.

ana: eviction semantics: hydrator handle should expose .release(reason) and a 'pin' API so runtime can hold critical tiles for KV priming. also need telemetry events for partial hydration latency and decode cost.

maria.p: agreed. telemetry: emit events: descriptor-read, tile-fetch, decode-start/decode-end, materialize, eviction. these feed Optimize recommendations.

build-bot: ci/loader-tests #42 failed on 'streamable-manifest' branch: flakey S3 range mock. see https://ci.internal/42

sanjay.k: i'll look into the mock failures. unrelated to api shape but blocks verification.

kevin_h: a nit: for quantized tiles we should allow 'deferred-dequant' — store quantized bytes in host and dequant on device if memory+latency permits. hydrator config could include profile hints.

maria.p: exactly. hydratorConfig = { lanePriorities, maxPinnedBytes, deferredDequantThreshold } . sketch:

maria.p: ```json
{
  "lanePriorities": {"hot":100,"warm":50,"cold":10},
  "maxPinnedBytes": 2147483648,
  "deferredDequantThreshold": 262144
}
```

ana: we need to define backpressure: when many requests pin hot tiles, fallback to creating ephemeral temp handles that can be regenerated. also a graceful fallback path to 'compatible lower-precision variant' if hydration can't finish in time.

sanjay.k: fallback to lower-precision variant is big — implies routing logic at request time. but good to surface as an optional policy per model.

maria.p: plan of action:
- ana: spec eviction/pin API and telemetry events
- kevin: draft hydrator interface + example shim for current loader
- sanjay: fix CI and prototype streamable manifest header reader
- ana + kevin: coordinate on async memory accounting
- i'll open a follow-up RFC PR with examples and perf expectations

ana: noted, will start a PR for the API draft.

kevin_h: i'll create a minimal shim that adapts current prefetcher to the hydrator interface so we can run A/B tests.

sanjay.k: i'll try to repro the CI flake and add a range-test harness.

maria.p: thanks all. one last ask: try to avoid renaming 'manifest' everywhere in codebase — keep 'manifest' as the on-disk index term, stream-friendly header = 'envelope' to reduce churn.

ana: ack

kevin_h: ack

build-bot: ci/loader-tests #42 rerun queued by @sanjay.k
